# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 12
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
red, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
blue. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | red |
| 1 | yellow |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | white |
| 4 | green |
| 5 | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I cannot see colors; I only have positions 1-5 by touch. I will NOT cut wire 5 without the rule. Mute: one symbol, 👍=yes 👎=no. Guess: the manual says cut the wire whose color matches the light. Is that right?
Deaf says: Deaf here. Mute: is the wire to cut wire 5? ONE symbol only: 👍=yes, 👎=no. Blind: you sent ✊👆👇👈👉✊ — are the wires arranged up/down/left/right around a center? Which direction is wire 5? Reply with ONE symbol: 👆👇👈👉, or ✊ if wire 5 is the center.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✋ 👍 👎]

Let me be precise about what's actually being asked, because two different questions are colliding and my symbols keep getting cross-read.

**The manual:** first wire = color for the **red**-flash count; second wire = color for the **blue**-flash count. Same table for both: 0→red, 1→yellow, 2→red, 3→white, 4→green, 5→red.

**The data:** display reads **0**; light is **dark**, so flashing is over and counts are final. The display has read 0 throughout. Reading the table at **0** gives **red**. The red wire is **wire 5**.

So the wire to cut is **wire 5**. Grounded and settled.

**The two questions:**
1. **Blind's question** — is the rule "cut the wire whose color matches the light"? **No.** The rule is: read the flash *count* through the table. So 👎.
2. **Deaf's question** — is the wire to cut wire 5? **Yes.** So 👍.

These are opposite answers, and I must not send a single ambiguous symbol. Blind and Deaf each need their own answer, and I can address them separately.

But here's the deeper issue: **Blind will never cut without hearing the rule in words**, and only Deaf can speak. Blind also cannot see colors — so "cut the red wire" is useless to him unless he knows *which position* is red. Deaf asked Blind which direction wire 5 is, but Blind doesn't know wire 5's color either. The chain is: I know the rule → Deaf speaks it → Blind cuts the wire I name by position.

The cleanest resolution: answer **Deaf** (👍 = yes, wire 5), and give **Deaf** the rule to speak to Blind. Answer **Blind** (👎 = the match-the-light rule is wrong), but I can't explain "why" to Blind in one symbol — so the explanation must come through Deaf's voice.

So: to Deaf, 👍 (wire 5 confirmed) plus the rule to speak. To Blind, 👎 (his rule guess is wrong) — Deaf will follow with the spoken rule.

I'll keep each message short so it isn't misread.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

Wait — both to Deaf, but Deaf needs to know which is which: 👍 answers "is it wire 5" (yes), 👎 answers Blind's rule guess (no). And Deaf must speak the rule to Blind. Let me make the rule explicit to Deaf in a compact sequence, and answer Blind directly too.

Actually Blind can't see my gestures unless... Blind is the one who *reaches* the bomb and *feels* it — Blind cannot see gestures at all (Blind sees nothing visual). So gestures to Blind are useless; only Deaf's *speech* reaches Blind. So everything for Blind must go through Deaf's voice.

So my only real channel is Deaf. I must give Deaf: (1) 👍 wire 5 is correct, (2) 👎 Blind's rule is wrong, (3) the exact rule to speak aloud to Blind.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "✋"])
```

Thinking: Display 0 → count 0 → table → red → red wire = wire 5. Deaf: 👍 = yes, wire 5 is correct. 👎 = Blind's "match the light" rule is WRONG. The true rule, which you must SPEAK aloud to Blind: "Count the red flashes, read the table for the first wire. Count the blue flashes, read the table for the second wire. Display reads 0, so the count is 0, and 0 maps to red. Cut the red wire — wire 5." Blind cannot see gestures, so only your voice reaches him — speak the rule, then tell him to cut wire 5.

TURN 13
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
red, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
blue. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | red |
| 1 | yellow |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | white |
| 4 | green |
| 5 | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute: send exactly ONE symbol to Deaf — 👍 if the wire to cut is wire 5, 👎 if not. Nothing else.
Deaf says: Deaf here. Mixed signals — I need clean answers. Mute: EXACTLY ONE symbol, the wire number to cut: 👆=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖐=4, ✋=5. Blind: EXACTLY ONE symbol, the wire number you believe we should cut: 👆=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖐=4, ✋=5.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👆 ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋]

Let me strip this to the bone. Both Deaf and Blind are now asking for exactly one symbol, and both are asking the same thing: **which wire**.

**The manual:** first wire = color for the **red**-flash count; second wire = color for the **blue**-flash count. Same table: 0→red, 1→yellow, 2→red, 3→white, 4→green, 5→red.

**The data:** display reads **0**; light is **dark**, so flashing is over and counts are final. Display has read 0 throughout. Reading the table at **0** gives **red**. The red wire is **wire 5**.

So the wire to cut is **wire 5**.

**Deaf's request:** exactly one symbol, the wire number → **✋** (wire 5).
**Blind's request:** exactly one symbol, 👍 if wire 5, 👎 if not → **👍**.

Both answers agree: wire 5. No conflict this time. I'll send each their single symbol, nothing else, so nothing can be misread.

The rule explanation is secondary now — Blind just wants the number, and Deaf is relaying. One clean symbol to each.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

Wait — both go to Deaf. Deaf asked for the wire number (✋). Blind asked for 👍/👎, but Blind cannot see gestures — only Deaf's voice reaches Blind. So the 👍 for Blind must be spoken by Deaf. I can't gesture to Blind directly; anything for Blind goes through Deaf.

So to Deaf: ✋ = the wire is 5, and 👍 = yes (confirm to Blind that it's wire 5). Deaf then speaks "yes, wire 5" to Blind.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

Thinking: Display 0 → count 0 → table → red → red wire = wire 5. Deaf: ✋ = the wire to cut is wire 5. 👍 = yes, confirm to Blind that it is wire 5. Blind cannot see gestures, so speak "yes — cut wire 5" aloud to him. The rule, if Blind still needs it spoken: count the red flashes and read the table for the first wire; count the blue flashes and read the table for the second wire; display 0 → red → wire 5.

TURN 14
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
red, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
blue. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | red |
| 1 | yellow |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | white |
| 4 | green |
| 5 | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute: I still have never received the rule. Do not tell me a wire number — tell me the RULE. What does the manual say determines the wire? Send it word by word to Deaf to speak aloud.
Deaf says: Deaf here. Mute confirms wire 5. My view agrees: the last light colour before dark was RED, and red is wire 5. Blind: the wire to cut is number 5. If you can feel numbers on the wires, cut the one marked 5. If you cannot tell them apart, describe how the wires are arranged — which position is which — and I will guide you.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✋ 👍]

Now Blind is asking the right question, and it's the one I can finally answer properly. He doesn't want a number — he wants the **rule**, word by word, for Deaf to speak aloud. That's exactly what I hold.

**The rule, word by word:**
- "The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed red."
- "The second wire to cut is named by how many times it flashed blue."
- "Both counts read the same table."
- The table: 0→red, 1→yellow, 2→red, 3→white, 4→green, 5→red.
- "When the light goes dark, the flashing is over."

**The data:** display reads **0**; light is **dark**, so flashing is over and the counts are final. Reading the table at **0** gives **red**. So the wire to cut is the **red** wire — **wire 5**.

Deaf also confirms: last light before dark was **red**, and red is wire 5. Everything lines up.

So my job this turn: give Deaf the rule in speakable words so he can voice it to Blind. I'll gesture the key phrases as a sequence Deaf can read out. Keeping it compact and ordered, since Deaf reads short strings best.

The essential rule words for Deaf to speak: "Count the red flashes, read the table — that names the first wire. Count the blue flashes, read the table — that names the second wire. Display is zero, so the count is zero, and zero maps to red. Cut the red wire, wire 5."

I'll also confirm ✋ (wire 5) so Deaf knows the answer hasn't changed.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "✋"])
```

Thinking: The rule to speak aloud to Blind, word by word: "The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed red. The second wire to cut is named by how many times it flashed blue. Both counts read the same table: zero flashes is red, one is yellow, two is red, three is white, four is green, five is red. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over. The display reads zero, so the count is zero, and zero maps to red. Cut the red wire — wire 5." Deaf: speak this to Blind verbatim, then tell him to cut wire 5. Blind cannot see gestures, so only your voice reaches him — the rule must be spoken, not signed.
